Definition: Percentage of the national population covered by at least one 4G/LTE mobile network signal, whether or not they subscribe to the service. 4G is the practical minimum for meaningful broadband connectivity enabling digital services.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Originally scored 0/Unknown with no source cited. A light check surfaced operator-reported coverage data suggesting this row was mislabelled, so it was escalated to full verification. Hormuud Telecom (Somalia's dominant mobile operator) stated in 2022 that over 70% of the population (~11.25m people) had access to 4G, with the government's National ICT Policy targeting full coverage by 2024-25; a March 2024 report reaffirmed 'approximately 70%' 4G population coverage, with plans to reach 88% urban/70% rural coverage. No independent GSMA Intelligence or ITU figure could be located to corroborate the operator's own claim, so the score rests on trade-press reporting of operator statements rather than an independently audited source. Recalculated from 0 to 3 (50-74%); flagged for human review given reliance on single-operator self-reported data.
revised_comments: Hormuud Telecom, Somalia's dominant mobile network operator, reports that approximately 70% of the national population is covered by its 4G network as of 2024, with plans to expand coverage to around 88% in urban areas and 70% in rural areas. The remaining population, concentrated in rural areas, relies on 2G/3G networks. The government's National ICT Policy targets full national 4G coverage by 2024-2025.

Definition: Whether the country has enacted legal or regulatory requirements mandating that certain categories of data (personal data, government data, financial data, or critical infrastructure data) be stored within national borders. Central to data sovereignty debates in Africa.
Comments: No authoritative evidence located on explicit data localisation requirements (beyond general cross-border transfer provisions in DPA) within budget.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Originally scored 0/Unknown, though the Comments already noted the DPA's cross-border transfer provisions. A light check confirmed authoritative sources exist, so the row was escalated to full verification. Somalia's Data Protection Act No. 005 of 2023 (in force since March 2023) establishes an adequacy-based cross-border transfer regime (Articles 30-31) requiring safeguards for transfers outside Somalia, but does not mandate that personal, government, financial, or critical infrastructure data be stored within national borders. No sector-specific data localisation law was identified; the Central Bank's Mobile Money Regulation (2020/2021) sets data security and business-continuity standards but not an in-country storage requirement. Recalculated from 0 to 1 (no data localisation requirements) rather than left as Unknown.
revised_comments: Somalia has no explicit data localisation requirement mandating that personal, government, financial, or critical infrastructure data be stored within its borders. The Data Protection Act No. 005 of 2023 and its implementing regulations establish an adequacy-based framework governing cross-border data transfers, requiring data controllers to ensure recipient jurisdictions or contractual safeguards afford adequate protection, but this falls short of a localisation mandate. Sector-specific rules, such as the Central Bank's Mobile Money Regulation, impose data security and continuity obligations without requiring in-country storage.

As of the most recent ministerial site visit in May 2025, the facility was reported to be nearing completion but not yet operational.

revision_notes: Originally scored 0/Unknown citing lack of Big Deal/Partech data. A light check found evidence of meaningful funding activity, so the row was escalated to full verification. Tracxn records over 560 Somalia-linked startups, of which 74 are funded, having collectively raised approximately $69.8m in venture capital/private equity since tracking began, including $16.3m raised in Q1 2026 alone across two rounds. Africa: The Big Deal's February 2026 funding roundup separately reports a $3m Y Combinator-backed seed round for Trace (Somalia). A dedicated accelerator/early-stage fund, Innovate Ventures, has operated since 2012. This is more consistent with a developing ecosystem with regular funding rounds than a nascent one, though funding volumes remain well short of the $50m+ annual threshold used for 'Established'. Recalculated from 0 to 3 (Developing); flagged for human review since Tracxn/Dealroom are secondary aggregators rather than the metadata's preferred primary sources (Partech, Disrupt Africa, Big Deal), and a precise annual (rather than cumulative) VC total specific to Somalia could not be confirmed.
revised_comments: Somalia has a developing but modest tech startup ecosystem. Tracxn records over 560 Somalia-linked startups, 74 of which have secured funding totalling around $69.8m in venture capital and private equity since tracking began, including $16.3m raised in the first quarter of 2026 across two rounds. Y Combinator-backed startups such as Trace have raised seed funding (a $3m round reported in February 2026), and a dedicated early-stage accelerator and fund, Innovate Ventures, has operated since 2012 supporting Somali startups. Funding activity, while regular, remains far below the levels seen in Africa's leading startup hubs.

A light check found direct evidence of multiple established universities offering diverse ICT/STEM programmes, so the row was escalated to full verification. At least four Somali universities maintain dedicated computer science/IT faculties: Mogadishu University (Faculty of Computer Science & IT, established 2003), Jazeera University (Faculty of Computer Science & IT, established 2010), City University of Mogadishu (Department of IT and Computer Science, offering Computer Science, IT/Information Security, and Telecoms/Networking degrees) and Hormuud University (seven distinct undergraduate programmes spanning Computer Science, Software Engineering, Cybersecurity, AI, Data Science, IoT and IT). No UNESCO UIS graduate-count or QS subject ranking was found, so enrolment scale and quality could not be independently benchmarked. Recalculated from 0 to 4 (established institutions with diverse ICT programmes) on the basis of institutional evidence; flagged for human review given the absence of enrolment/quality metrics to confirm the exact tier.
revised_comments: Somalia has several established universities offering diverse tertiary ICT and STEM programmes. Mogadishu University's Faculty of Computer Science and IT (established 2003) and Jazeera University's equivalent faculty (established 2010) are long-standing providers, while City University of Mogadishu offers Computer Science, Information Technology/Information Security and Telecommunications/Networking degrees, and Hormuud University offers seven distinct undergraduate tracks including Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Cybersecurity, the Internet of Things and Software Engineering. Enrolment figures and independent quality benchmarks, such as UNESCO graduate counts or QS subject rankings, are not published for these institutions.
